def: A signed, dated and notarized document in which a service user sets out treatment preferences ahead of time. It can be revoked by a new directive or a notarized revocation.
The biopsychosocial spiritual view used in AO 2025-0028, which sees a person across biological, psychological, social and spiritual dimensions.
A person, who may or may not be a relative, with a close personal relationship to the patient and concern for their welfare.
Community-based mental health: delivery of mental and neurological health services within a geographically defined community.
DOH Center for Health Development, the regional arm of the DOH. Under AO 2025-0028, CHDs give technical assistance to LGUs and consolidate local reports into quarterly regional summaries.

In AO 2025-0028, a trained person delivering mental and neurological health services in the community. The definition is broad, from barangay health workers to teachers, parents, workplace staff, volunteers and faith-based leaders.
Keeping information about a service user safe from access, use or disclosure by unauthorized persons. Disclosure without written consent is allowed only in the five cases in Section 5(l).
Moving service users from institutional and segregated settings into community-based settings that support social participation, recovery and individualized care.
Any distinction, exclusion or restriction that nullifies the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights on an equal basis, including denial of reasonable accommodation.

Health Care Provider Network: a public or private group of primary to tertiary providers giving integrated care, with the primary care provider as navigator. AO 2025-0028 uses it for referral to higher levels and back to the community.

term: Impairment or temporary loss of decision-making capacity
def: A medically determined inability to give informed consent, assessed by a mental health professional. The service user cannot understand their condition, the consequences of decisions, or the proposed treatment, or cannot communicate consent.
Consent voluntarily given to a treatment plan after full disclosure, in plain language, of its nature, consequences, benefits, risks and alternatives. The Act requires it in writing.
A board every public and private health facility must set up to review cases about treatment, restraint and confinement. It includes a DOH representative and a CHR representative.
Local Investment Plan for Health, the local plan into which AO 2025-0028 requires LGUs to integrate their CBMH strategies and action plans.
A person designated by the service user, appointed by a court or authorized by law to act on the user's behalf, including as substitute decision maker during temporary impairment of capacity.
The Mental Health Gap Action Programme, a WHO training program. AO 2025-0028 expects basic services to be delivered by mhGAP-trained primary care providers.
Mental Health Information System, where AO 2025-0028 says patient data are to be recorded.

Mental Health and Psychosocial Support. AO 2016-0039 gives the Health Emergency Management Bureau the lead on MHPSS in disasters and emergencies, and AO 2025-0028 lists MHPSS among community crisis services.
Mental, neurological and substance use disorders, the term AO 2016-0039 uses for its program.

A condition presenting a serious and immediate threat to the health and well-being of a service user or others, needing immediate medical intervention. It is one of the two triggers for the consent exceptions in Section 13.
Care centered on the service user's strengths, with people with lived experience as equal partners and the user's own understanding built into the treatment plan.
A person with lived experience of any mental health condition, including people who need or are undergoing psychiatric, neurologic or psychosocial care.
Helping a service user who has capacity to express a preference or decision. Under the Act a user may name up to three supporters.
Training non-specialist providers in the community to provide mental health care, especially in areas that lack resources.

Two of the three strategic approaches of the National Mental Health Program in AO 2016-0039. The first is government leadership across institutions, law, finance and services. The second brings in civil society, service-user groups, families and providers.
